title: How AI Could Reinforce Dollar Dominance
gist: Truncated commentary opening: Fu and Huang argue that AI companies, cloud providers and payment networks are quietly writing the next chapter of dollar dominance, because compute — a critical input for the global economy — is being priced, paid for and recycled into dollar assets via long-dated data-center leases and dollar-pegged stablecoins tied to the AI boom.

insights.claim: A 20-year data-center lease should be read as a monetary event, because compute contracts denominate and settle a critical input for the global economy and recycle the proceeds into dollar assets.
insights.speaker: Chenxu Fu
insights.so_what: Long-dated compute contracts are a new structural source of dollar demand — track lease and offtake currency denomination as a reserve-currency indicator.
insights.quote: such developments are proliferating—and contributing to the formation of a system in which a critical input for the global economy is priced, paid for, and ultimately recycled into dollar assets
insights.locator: SINGAPORE—The signing of a 20-year data-center lease

insights.claim: Dollar-pegged stablecoins linked to the AI boom are among the proliferating developments building a compute-settlement system anchored in the dollar.
insights.speaker: Chenxu Fu
insights.so_what: Ties stablecoin issuance growth to AI capex rather than only to crypto trading — a second demand channel for short-dated dollar assets.
insights.locator: SINGAPORE—The signing of a 20-year data-center lease

insights.claim: The future of dollar dominance is being determined in practice by AI companies, cloud providers and payment networks rather than by the policymakers and economists debating it.
insights.speaker: Chenxu Fu
insights.so_what: De-dollarization analysis that ignores compute contracting and payment rails is looking in the wrong place; corporate plumbing beats central-bank rhetoric.
insights.quote: AI companies, cloud providers, and payment networks might already be writing it into the next chapter of international monetary history
insights.locator: While policymakers and economists debate the future of dollar dominance

insights.claim: Actors hoping to shape the next chapter of international monetary history must act now or risk being excluded entirely, because the compute-settlement architecture is being locked in as it is built.
insights.speaker: Chenxu Fu
insights.so_what: Implies a closing window for non-dollar compute settlement rails — watch for euro-, yuan- or local-currency compute contracting initiatives as the counter-move.
insights.quote: Those who hope to shape that chapter must act now—or risk being left off the page.
insights.locator: While policymakers and economists debate the future of dollar dominance
